points.quote: Its virtual runtime grows to 13.0 and it goes back in after 12.4
points.problem: The process runs from 3.2 up to 13.0, past 8.1, 10.0 and 12.4, which contradicts the stated rule that the scheduler always runs whoever has had least. A real CFS turn ends once the running task's vruntime passes the next-smallest, so it would go back in near 8.1, not beyond 12.4.
points.hint: Use a smaller growth (e.g. 3.2 to 8.6, goes back after 8.1) or say the figure exaggerates the turn.

points.quote: is still the language of every production kernel
points.problem: Overclaim: kernels such as XNU's IOKit use C++, Windows has C++ parts, and Linux now accepts Rust code; only 'most' or 'the core of the major kernels' holds.
points.hint: Say 'the language of the kernels we have just read' or 'of Linux and its kin'.
